title: An Evolutionary Analysis of Narrative Selection
abstract: arXiv:2508.03540v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: We compare the evolutionary selection of agents who employ different heuristics to select the narratives through which they interpret new information. Agents' survival depends on the accuracy of their beliefs. Agents who choose narratives to align with the population's average belief have higher survival rates than those who use alternative heuristics. Conforming reduces an agent's belief variance but inherits the bias of the average belief, so it pays when the latter is close to the state's probability. Evolutionary selection helps maintain this proximity by eliminating inaccurate agents. The other heuristics survive as well, with their shares depending on the degree of uncertainty: agents who tend to form mild beliefs survive more when uncertainty is high, whereas those who tend to form extreme beliefs survive more when uncertainty is low. Conformism is usually considered detrimental, as it discards private information. In our mode

translated_abstract: 我们比较了采用不同启发式方法来选择叙事以解读新信息的智能体在演化中的选择过程。智能体的生存取决于其信念的准确性。选择与群体平均信念保持一致的叙事的智能体，比使用其他启发式方法的智能体具有更高的生存率。从众会降低智能体的信念方差，但会继承平均信念中存在的偏差，因此当平均信念接近状态的真实概率时，从众是有利的。演化选择通过淘汰不准确的智能体来帮助维持这种接近性。其他启发式方法同样能够生存下来，其占比取决于不确定性的程度：当不确定性较高时，倾向于形成温和信念的智能体存活率更高；而当不确定性较低时，倾向于形成极端信念的智能体存活率更高。从众通常被认为是有害的，因为它会丢弃私人信息。在我们的模型中……
tldr: 该论文通过演化模型分析发现，在选择解读新信息的叙事时，与群体平均信念保持从众一致的策略具有最高的生存率，且形成温和信念的策略在高不确定性下更有优势，形成极端信念的策略在低不确定性下更有优势。
en_tdlr: Using an evolutionary model, this paper shows that conformism in narrative selection yields the highest survival rates, while mild beliefs survive better under high uncertainty and extreme beliefs under low uncertainty.
